{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01F52s4pfgrG7t2S2vnPuw9h","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Lexical Agent Guide\n2\t\n3\tThis file provides detailed guidance for AI agents and automated tools working with the Lexical codebase.\n4\t\n5\t## Build, Test, and Development Commands\n6\t\n7\t### Building\n8\t- `pnpm run build` - Build all packages in development mode\n9\t- `pnpm run build-prod` - Clean and build all packages in production mode\n10\t- `pnpm run build-release` - Build production release with error codes\n11\t- `pnpm run build-types` - Build TypeScript type definitions and validate them\n12\t\n13\t### Testing\n14\t- `pnpm run test-unit` - Run all unit tests (Vitest, jsdom)\n15\t- `pnpm run test-unit-watch` - Run unit tests in watch mode\n16\t- `pnpm run test-browser` - Run browser-mode unit tests (Vitest + Playwright, real browser)\n17\t- `pnpm run test-browser-watch` - Run browser-mode tests in watch mode\n18\t- `pnpm run test-e2e-chromium` - Run E2E tests in Chromium (requires dev server running)\n19\t- `pnpm run test-e2e-firefox` - Run E2E tests in Firefox\n20\t- `pnpm run test-e2e-webkit` - Run E2E tests in WebKit\n21\t- `pnpm run debug-test-e2e-chromium` - Run E2E tests in debug mode (headed)\n22\t- `pnpm run debug-test-unit` - Debug unit tests with inspector\n23\t\n24\tFor E2E testing workflow:\n25\t1. Start the dev server: `pnpm run start` (or `pnpm run dev` if you don't need collab)\n26\t2. In another terminal: `pnpm run test-e2e-chromium`\n27\t\n28\t### Development Servers\n29\t- `pnpm run start` - Start playground dev server + collab server (http://localhost:3000)\n30\t- `pnpm run dev` - Start only the playground dev server (no collab)\n31\t- `pnpm run start:website` - Start Docusaurus website (http://localhost:3001)\n32\t- `pnpm run collab` - Start collab server on localhost:1234\n33\t\n34\t### Code Quality\n35\t- `pnpm run lint` - Run ESLint on all files\n36\t- `pnpm run lint:fix` - Auto-fix lint issues\n37\t- `pnpm run prettier` - Check code formatting\n38\t- `pnpm run prettier:fix` - Auto-fix formatting issues\n39\t- `pnpm run flow` - Run Flow type checker\n40\t- `pnpm run tsc` - Run TypeScript compiler\n41\t- `pnpm run ci-check` - Run all checks (TypeScript, Flow, Prettier, ESLint)\n42\t\n43\t### Tree-shaking annotations\n44\t\n45\tModule-scope calls to the side-effect-free factories (`defineExtension`,\n46\t`configExtension`, `safeCast`, `createCommand`, `createState`,\n47\t`defineImportRule`, etc.) must be annotated with `/* @__PURE__ */` so\n48\tbundlers can drop unused definitions from application bundles. This is\n49\tenforced (with an autofixer) by the\n50\t`@lexical/internal/require-pure-annotation` ESLint rule — run\n51\t`pnpm run lint:fix` (also run by the pre-commit hook) to insert the\n52\tannotations automatically. When adding a new factory of this kind,\n53\tannotate its definition with `@__NO_SIDE_EFFECTS__` and add its name to\n54\tthe rule's default list in\n55\t`packages/lexical-eslint-plugin-internal/src/rules/require-pure-annotation.js`.\n56\t\n57\t## High-Level Architecture\n58\t\n59\t### Core Concepts\n60\t\n61\tLexical is built around several key architectural concepts that work together:\n62\t\n63\t**Editor Instance** - Created via `createEditor()`, wires everything together. Manages the EditorState, registers listeners/commands/transforms, and handles DOM reconciliation.\n64\t\n65\t**EditorState** - Immutable data model representing the editor content. Contains:\n66\t- A node tree (hierarchical structure of LexicalNodes)\n67\t- A selection object (current cursor/selection state)\n68\t- Fully serializable to/from JSON\n69\t\n70\t**`$` Functions Convention** - Functions prefixed with `$` (e.g., `$getRoot()`, `$getSelection()`) can ONLY be called within:\n71\t- `editor.update(() => {...})` - for mutations\n72\t- `editor.read(() => {...})` - for read-only access\n73\t- Node transforms and command handlers (which have implicit update context)\n74\t\n75\tThis is similar to React hooks' restrictions but enforces synchronous context instead of call order.\n76\t\n77\t**Double-Buffering Updates** - When `editor.update()` is called:\n78\t1. Current EditorState is cloned as work-in-progress\n79\t2. Mutations modify the work-in-progress state\n80\t3. Multiple synchronous updates are batched\n81\t4. DOM reconciler diffs and applies changes\n82\t5. New immutable EditorState becomes current\n83\t\n84\t**Node Immutability & Keys** - All nodes are recursively frozen after reconciliation. Node methods automatically call `node.getWritable()` to create mutable clones. All versions of a logical node share the same runtime-only key, allowing node methods to always reference the latest version from the active EditorState.\n85\t\n86\t### Monorepo Structure\n87\t\n88\tThis is a monorepo with packages in `packages/`:\n89\t\n90\t**Core Packages:**\n91\t- `lexical` - Core framework (Editor, EditorState, base nodes, selection, updates)\n92\t- `@lexical/react` - React bindings (LexicalComposer, plugins as components)\n93\t- `@lexical/headless` - Headless editor for server-side/testing\n94\t\n95\t**Feature Packages** (extend core with nodes/commands/utilities):\n96\t- `@lexical/rich-text` - Rich text editing (headings, quotes, etc.)\n97\t- `@lexical/plain-text` - Plain text editing\n98\t- `@lexical/extension` - Extend editor functionality\n99\t- `@lexical/list` - List nodes (ordered/unordered/checklist)\n100\t- `@lexical/table` - Table support\n101\t- `@lexical/code` - Code block with syntax highlighting\n102\t- `@lexical/link` - Link nodes and utilities\n103\t- `@lexical/markdown` - Markdown import/export\n104\t- `@lexical/html` - HTML serialization\n105\t- `@lexical/history` - Undo/redo\n106\t- `@lexical/yjs` - Real-time collaboration via Yjs\n107\t- And many more...\n108\t\n109\t**Development Packages:**\n110\t- `lexical-playground` - Full-featured demo application\n111\t- `lexical-website` - Docusaurus documentation site\n112\t\n113\t### Key Architectural Patterns\n114\t\n115\t**Extensions** - Extensions should be used to add features and configuration\n116\tto an editor. The set of extensions in an editor must be determined when the\n117\teditor is created with `buildEditorFromExtensions`. Extensions with\n118\tfunctionality that can be toggled on or off typically have a `disabled`\n119\tconfiguration property and output signal that defaults to `false`. See the\n120\tlexical-extension package and the supporting code in lexical for\n121\tmore examples and implementation details.\n122\t\n123\t```tsx\n124\texport interface MyConfig {\n125\t  disabled: boolean;\n126\t}\n127\texport const MyExtension = defineExtension({\n128\t  build: (_editor, config, _state) => namedSignals(config),\n129\t  config: safeCast<MyConfig>({ disabled: false }),\n130\t  name: '@lexical/docs/My',\n131\t  nodes: () => [MyNode],\n132\t  register: (editor, _config, state) => {\n133\t    const {disabled} = state.getOutput();\n134\t    return effect(() => {\n135\t      if (!disabled.value) {\n136\t        return editor.registerUpdateListener(({editorState}) => {\n137\t          // React to updates\n138\t        });\n139\t      }\n140\t    })\n141\t  },\n142\t})\n143\t```\n144\t\n145\t**Plugin System (React)** - Plugins are a legacy pattern for React components\n146\tto hook into the editor lifecycle, extensions should be preferred for new code:\n147\t```jsx\n148\tfunction MyPlugin() {\n149\t  const [editor] = useLexicalComposerContext();\n150\t  useEffect(() => {\n151\t    return editor.registerUpdateListener(({editorState}) => {\n152\t      // React to updates\n153\t    });\n154\t  }, [editor]);\n155\t  return null;\n156\t}\n157\t```\n158\t\n159\t**Command Pattern** - Commands are the primary communication mechanism:\n160\t- Create with `createCommand()`\n161\t- Dispatch with `editor.dispatchCommand(command, payload)`\n162\t- Handle with `editor.registerCommand(command, handler, priority)`\n163\t- Handlers propagate by priority until one stops propagation\n164\t\n165\t**Node Transforms** - Registered via `editor.registerNodeTransform(NodeClass, transform)`. Called automatically during updates when nodes of that type change. Have implicit update context.\n166\t\n167\t**Listeners** - All `editor.register*()` methods return cleanup functions for easy unsubscription.\n168\t\n169\t## Type System\n170\t\n171\tThis codebase uses **both TypeScript and Flow**:\n172\t- Source files are primarily TypeScript (`.ts`, `.tsx`)\n173\t- Flow type definitions are generated in `packages/*/flow/` directories\n174\t- Run `pnpm run flow` to check Flow types\n175\t- Run `pnpm run tsc` to check TypeScript types\n176\t- Both are checked in CI via `pnpm run ci-check`\n177\t\n178\tWhen adding/modifying APIs, types must be maintained for both systems.\n179\t\n180\t## Backwards Compatibility\n181\t\n182\t**All changes MUST be backwards compatible.** Lexical is a widely-adopted OSS library, and breaking changes ripple out to every downstream consumer.\n183\t\n184\t- Do NOT remove or rename existing public APIs, exported functions, types, or `$` functions. Add new APIs alongside the old ones instead.\n185\t- Do NOT change the signature, return type, or behavior of existing public APIs in ways that could break callers. Prefer additive, optional parameters.\n186\t- Preserve the serialization format of `EditorState` and node JSON. Serialized content produced by older versions must continue to deserialize correctly.\n187\t- If an API genuinely must change, deprecate the old one first (keep it working, document the replacement) rather than removing it outright.\n188\t- When in doubt, assume external code depends on the current behavior and keep it intact.\n189\t\n190\t## Important Development Notes\n191\t\n192\t### Reconciliation and Updates\n193\t- `editor.read(...)`  or `editor.read('force-commit', ...)` flushes pending updates first, then provides consistent reconciled state\n194\t- `editor.read('pending', ...)` reads the pending state (like `editor.update(...)`, but read-only)\n195\t- `editor.read('latest', ...)` reads the latest consistent reconciled state\n196\t- Inside `editor.update()`, you see pending state (transforms/reconciliation not yet run)\n197\t- `editor.getEditorState().read()` always uses latest reconciled state, but prefer `editor.read('latest', ...)` in new code\n198\t- Updates can be nested: `editor.update(() => editor.update(...))` is allowed but strongly discouraged\n199\t- Do NOT nest updates in reads, or use a force-commit in an update\n200\t\n201\t### Node References\n202\tAlways access node properties/methods within read/update context. Nodes automatically resolve to their latest version via their key. Don't store node references across update boundaries.\n203\t\n204\t### Testing Strategy\n205\t- **Unit tests** - Vitest (jsdom), located in `packages/**/__tests__/unit/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}`\n206\t- **Browser tests** - Vitest browser mode driven by the Playwright runner, located in\n207\t  `packages/**/__tests__/browser/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}`. Use these for behavior that depends on\n208\t  a real layout/selection engine instead of stubbing the missing jsdom functionality from\n209\t  `vitest.setup.mts` (e.g. `Range.getBoundingClientRect`, the Selection API). Run with\n210\t  `pnpm run test-browser`; the browser set is controlled by the `VITEST_BROWSER` env var\n211\t  (comma-separated, default `chromium`). Prefer building editors with the extension APIs\n212\t  (`buildEditorFromExtensions`, or `LexicalExtensionComposer`/`LexicalExtensionEditorComposer`\n213\t  in React).\n214\t  - **Do not use `using`/`Disposable` in browser tests (or any browser-facing code).**\n215\t    Explicit Resource Management (`using`, `Symbol.dispose`, `Disposable`) is not supported\n216\t    in WebKit/Safari yet, so the syntax throws a `SyntaxError` there. `using` is fine in unit\n217\t    tests (jsdom/Node), but browser tests should clean up with\n218\t    `onTestFinished(() => editor.dispose())` instead — `editor.dispose()` is a plain method\n219\t    available on the result of `buildEditorFromExtensions`.\n220\t- **E2E tests** - Playwright, located in `packages/lexical-playground/__tests__/e2e/**/*.spec.{ts,mjs}`\n221\t- E2E tests require the playground dev server running\n222\t- Use `pnpm run debug-test-e2e-chromium` to debug E2E tests with browser UI\n223\t\n224\t### Custom Nodes\n225\tWhen creating custom nodes:\n226\t1. Extend a base node class (TextNode, ElementNode, DecoratorNode)\n227\t2. Implement instance methods: `$config()`, `createDOM()`, `updateDOM()`\n228\t3. Register with extension or editor config: `nodes: [YourCustomNode]`\n229\t4. Export a `$createYourNode()` factory function (follows $ convention)\n230\t\n231\t### Build System\n232\t- Uses Rollup for bundling\n233\t- Build script: `scripts/build.mjs`\n234\t- Supports multiple build modes: development, production, www (Meta internal)\n235\t- TypeScript source → compiled to CommonJS and ESM\n236\t- Package manager logic in `scripts/shared/packagesManager.mjs`\n237\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"16879198-52f9-4498-8679-78929c8d4ba7","uuid":"6456d345-817e-4f16-8e69-923c850ff2a2","timestamp":"2026-08-21T20:42:06.827Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/app/AGENTS.md","content":"# Lexical Agent Guide\n\nThis file provides detailed guidance for AI agents and automated tools working with the Lexical codebase.\n\n## Build, Test, and Development Commands\n\n### Building\n- `pnpm run build` - Build all packages in development mode\n- `pnpm run build-prod` - Clean and build all packages in production mode\n- `pnpm run build-release` - Build production release with error codes\n- `pnpm run build-types` - Build TypeScript type definitions and validate them\n\n### Testing\n- `pnpm run test-unit` - Run all unit tests (Vitest, jsdom)\n- `pnpm run test-unit-watch` - Run unit tests in watch mode\n- `pnpm run test-browser` - Run browser-mode unit tests (Vitest + Playwright, real browser)\n- `pnpm run test-browser-watch` - Run browser-mode tests in watch mode\n- `pnpm run test-e2e-chromium` - Run E2E tests in Chromium (requires dev server running)\n- `pnpm run test-e2e-firefox` - Run E2E tests in Firefox\n- `pnpm run test-e2e-webkit` - Run E2E tests in WebKit\n- `pnpm run debug-test-e2e-chromium` - Run E2E tests in debug mode (headed)\n- `pnpm run debug-test-unit` - Debug unit tests with inspector\n\nFor E2E testing workflow:\n1. New immutable EditorState becomes current\n\n**Node Immutability & Keys** - All nodes are recursively frozen after reconciliation. Node methods automatically call `node.getWritable()` to create mutable clones. All versions of a logical node share the same runtime-only key, allowing node methods to always reference the latest version from the active EditorState.\n\n### Monorepo Structure\n\nThis is a monorepo with packages in `packages/`:\n\n**Core Packages:**\n- `lexical` - Core framework (Editor, EditorState, base nodes, selection, updates)\n- `@lexical/react` - React bindings (LexicalComposer, plugins as components)\n- `@lexical/headless` - Headless editor for server-side/testing\n\n**Feature Packages** (extend core with nodes/commands/utilities):\n- `@lexical/rich-text` - Rich text editing (headings, quotes, etc.)\n- `@lexical/plain-text` - Plain text editing\n- `@lexical/extension` - Extend editor functionality\n- `@lexical/list` - List nodes (ordered/unordered/checklist)\n- `@lexical/table` - Table support\n- `@lexical/code` - Code block with syntax highlighting\n- `@lexical/link` - Link nodes and utilities\n- `@lexical/markdown` - Markdown import/export\n- `@lexical/html` - HTML serialization\n- `@lexical/history` - Undo/redo\n- `@lexical/yjs` - Real-time collaboration via Yjs\n- And many more...\n\n**Development Packages:**\n- `lexical-playground` - Full-featured demo application\n- `lexical-website` - Docusaurus documentation site\n\n### Key Architectural Patterns\n\n**Extensions** - Extensions should be used to add features and configuration\nto an editor. The set of extensions in an editor must be determined when the\neditor is created with `buildEditorFromExtensions`. Extensions with\nfunctionality that can be toggled on or off typically have a `disabled`\nconfiguration property and output signal that defaults to `false`. See the\nlexical-extension package and the supporting code in lexical for\nmore examples and implementation details.\n\n```tsx\nexport interface MyConfig {\n  disabled: boolean;\n}\nexport const MyExtension = defineExtension({\n  build: (_editor, config, _state) => namedSignals(config),\n  config: safeCast<MyConfig>({ disabled: false }),\n  name: '@lexical/docs/My',\n  nodes: () => [MyNode],\n  register: (editor, _config, state) => {\n    const {disabled} = state.getOutput();\n    return effect(() => {\n      if (!disabled.value) {\n        return editor.registerUpdateListener(({editorState}) => {\n          // React to updates\n        });\n      }\n    })\n  },\n})\n```\n\n**Plugin System (React)** - Plugins are a legacy pattern for React components\nto hook into the editor lifecycle, extensions should be preferred for new code:\n```jsx\nfunction MyPlugin() {\n  const [editor] = useLexicalComposerContext();\n  useEffect(() => {\n    return editor.registerUpdateListener(({editorState}) => {\n      // React to updates\n    });\n  }, [editor]);\n  return null;\n}\n```\n\n**Command Pattern** - Commands are the primary communication mechanism:\n- Create with `createCommand()`\n- Dispatch with `editor.dispatchCommand(command, payload)`\n- Handle with `editor.registerCommand(command, handler, priority)`\n- Handlers propagate by priority until one stops propagation\n\n**Node Transforms** - Registered via `editor.registerNodeTransform(NodeClass, transform)`. Called automatically during updates when nodes of that type change. Have implicit update context.\n\n**Listeners** - All `editor.register*()` methods return cleanup functions for easy unsubscription.\n\n## Type System\n\nThis codebase uses **both TypeScript and Flow**:\n- Source files are primarily TypeScript (`.ts`, `.tsx`)\n- Flow type definitions are generated in `packages/*/flow/` directories\n- Run `pnpm run flow` to check Flow types\n- Run `pnpm run tsc` to check TypeScript types\n- Both are checked in CI via `pnpm run ci-check`\n\nWhen adding/modifying APIs, types must be maintained for both systems.\n\n## Backwards Compatibility\n\n**All changes MUST be backwards compatible.** Lexical is a widely-adopted OSS library, and breaking changes ripple out to every downstream consumer.\n\n- Do NOT remove or rename existing public APIs, exported functions, types, or `$` functions. Add new APIs alongside the old ones instead.\n- Do NOT change the signature, return type, or behavior of existing public APIs in ways that could break callers. Prefer additive, optional parameters.\n- Preserve the serialization format of `EditorState` and node JSON. Serialized content produced by older versions must continue to deserialize correctly.\n- If an API genuinely must change, deprecate the old one first (keep it working, document the replacement) rather than removing it outright.\n- When in doubt, assume external code depends on the current behavior and keep it intact.\n\n## Important Development Notes\n\n### Reconciliation and Updates\n- `editor.read(...)`  or `editor.read('force-commit', ...)` flushes pending updates first, then provides consistent reconciled state\n- `editor.read('pending', ...)` reads the pending state (like `editor.update(...)`, but read-only)\n- `editor.read('latest', ...)` reads the latest consistent reconciled state\n- Inside `editor.update()`, you see pending state (transforms/reconciliation not yet run)\n- `editor.getEditorState().read()` always uses latest reconciled state, but prefer `editor.read('latest', ...)` in new code\n- Updates can be nested: `editor.update(() => editor.update(...))` is allowed but strongly discouraged\n- Do NOT nest updates in reads, or use a force-commit in an update\n\n### Node References\nAlways access node properties/methods within read/update context. Nodes automatically resolve to their latest version via their key. Don't store node references across update boundaries.\n\n### Testing Strategy\n- **Unit tests** - Vitest (jsdom), located in `packages/**/__tests__/unit/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}`\n- **Browser tests** - Vitest browser mode driven by the Playwright runner, located in\n  `packages/**/__tests__/browser/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}`. Use these for behavior that depends on\n  a real layout/selection engine instead of stubbing the missing jsdom functionality from\n  `vitest.setup.mts` (e.g. `Range.getBoundingClientRect`, the Selection API). Run with\n  `pnpm run test-browser`; the browser set is controlled by the `VITEST_BROWSER` env var\n  (comma-separated, default `chromium`). Prefer building editors with the extension APIs\n  (`buildEditorFromExtensions`, or `LexicalExtensionComposer`/`LexicalExtensionEditorComposer`\n  in React).\n  - **Do not use `using`/`Disposable` in browser tests (or any browser-facing code).**\n    Explicit Resource Management (`using`, `Symbol.dispose`, `Disposable`) is not supported\n    in WebKit/Safari yet, so the syntax throws a `SyntaxError` there. `using` is fine in unit\n    tests (jsdom/Node), but browser tests should clean up with\n    `onTestFinished(() => editor.dispose())` instead — `editor.dispose()` is a plain method\n    available on the result of `buildEditorFromExtensions`.\n- **E2E tests** - Playwright, located in `packages/lexical-playground/__tests__/e2e/**/*.spec.{ts,mjs}`\n- E2E tests require the playground dev server running\n- Use `pnpm run debug-test-e2e-chromium` to debug E2E tests with browser UI\n\n### Custom Nodes\nWhen creating custom nodes:\n1. Extend a base node class (TextNode, ElementNode, DecoratorNode)\n2. Implement instance methods: `$config()`, `createDOM()`, `updateDOM()`\n3. Register with extension or editor config: `nodes: [YourCustomNode]`\n4. Export a `$createYourNode()` factory function (follows $ convention)\n\n### Build System\n- Uses Rollup for bundling\n- Build script: `scripts/build.mjs`\n- Supports multiple build modes: development, production, www (Meta internal)\n- TypeScript source → compiled to CommonJS and ESM\n- Package manager logic in `scripts/shared/packagesManager.mjs`\n","numLines":237,"startLine":1,"totalLines":237}}}

  const chip = editor.getEditorState()._nodeMap.get(chipKey) as ChipNode;\n        const textFormat = (\n          editor.getEditorState()._nodeMap.get(textKey) as import('lexical').TextNode\n        ).getFormat();\n        // The single Bold action must leave the chip and the text with the\n        // same bold state — never one formatted and the other not.\n        expect(chip.hasFormat('bold')).toBe((textFormat & IS_BOLD) !== 0);\n      });\n    },\n  );\n\n  test('makes a mixed selection all bold in one action', () => {\n    const editor = setUpEditor();\n    let chipKey = '';\n    let textKey = '';\n    // Chip already bold, text plain: pressing Bold should make BOTH bold.\n    editor.update(\n      () => {\n        ({chipKey, textKey} = });\n});\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":26,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2001,"cache_read_input_tokens":80192,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":2001,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0},"output_tokens":2,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global"},"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"16879198-52f9-4498-8679-78929c8d4ba7","uuid":"ff341f67-8327-4e60-b0ed-c7eacdc461f2","timestamp":"2026-08-21T20:49:10.702Z"}

const DecoratorTextExtension = /* @__PURE__ */ defineExtension({\n  name: '@lexical/extension/DecoratorText',\n  nodes: () => [DecoratorTextNode],\n  register(editor, config, state) {\n    return editor.registerCommand<TextFormatType>(\n      FORMAT_TEXT_COMMAND,\n      formatType => {\n        const selection = $getSelection();\n        if (!$isNodeSelection(selection) && !$isRangeSelection(selection)) {\n          return false;\n        }\n        const nodes = selection.getNodes();\n        // Mirror RangeSelection.formatText: the format direction is driven by\n independently (which can leave part of a\n        // mixed selection unformatted). {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-8","id":"msg_011CeGZ84MY4yWAQw7kYdmJk","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The fix is in place and verified. Here's a summary of the work.\n\n## The bug\n\nSelecting an inline chip (the `DateTimeNode` \"Sat Jun 20 2026\" pill) together with adjacent plain text and pressing **Bold** formats only one part — the chip is \"left unformatted\" while the text changes (or vice-versa). Plain text alone always works.\n\n## Root cause\n\nThe chip is a `DecoratorTextNode` (a `DecoratorNode`, **not** a `TextNode`), so it stores its own format and is formatted out-of-band. `FORMAT_TEXT_COMMAND` is handled by **two independent listeners** that both run for one keypress:\n\n1. **`@lexical/rich-text`** (`COMMAND_PRIORITY_EDITOR`) → `RangeSelection.formatText()`. It skips non-text nodes and formats text with **alignment** — the direction is decided by the first text node and everything converges to it.\n2. **`DecoratorTextExtension`** (`COMMAND_PRIORITY_LOW`, runs first) → naively called `node.toggleFormat()` on each chip, deciding direction from the chip's *own* current format with **no alignment**.\n\nWhen the chip and the text start with different bold states, the two handlers move in **opposite directions**, so a single Bold press fails to make both parts consistent. (`packages/lexical/src/LexicalUpdates.ts:917` confirms priorities dispatch 4→0, so the extension runs before rich-text and, returning `false`, both execute.)\n\n## The fix\n\n`packages/lexical-extension/src/DecoratorTextExtension.ts` — the extension now mirrors `formatText`'s alignment: it computes the target format from the first `TextNode` in the selection and aligns every decorator node to it (falling back to the first decorator when the selection has no text, e.g. a pure `NodeSelection` of chips).
